author: magmueller
body: Replaces browser-script-based highlighting with a Python-based solution to improve performance and add flexible highlighting controls. The previous approach injected JavaScript into the browser for highlighting, which introduced delays and prevented parallel execution of screenshot capture and DOM processing. This PR moves highlighting to Python, allowing these operations to run concurrently and providing more granular control over the visual output, such as color-coding by element type and filtering by index. --- [Slack Thread](https://browser-use.slack.com/archives/D092QUQD6KA/p1755390842442949?thread_ts=1755390842.442949&cid=D092QUQD6KA) --- ## Summary by cubic Replaced browser-injected JS highlights with a fast Python/Pillow highlighter to enable parallel screenshot capture and DOM processing and add flexible controls. The agent now returns highlighted screenshots by default without extra latency. - New Features - Python-based highlighting: color-coded boxes by element type, index labels, include/exclude filters. - BrowserStateSummary helpers: get_highlighted_screenshot and get_image_pair, with caching when no filters are used. - MCP updates: new browser_get_highlighted_screenshot tool; browser_get_state now also returns a highlighted screenshot. - Removed script injection and highlight cleanup; fewer roundtrips and better performance. - Example: examples/test_highlighting.py demonstrates usage.

author: google-labs-jules[bot]
body: This commit fixes a bug where the playback duration would not update immediately after being changed. The issue was caused by a stale closure in the `webPlayback.tsx` component, which prevented the player from using the latest track settings. The fix involves using a `useRef` to ensure the event listener always has access to the most recent `handleState` function.

author: copilot
body:
Thanks for assigning this issue to me. I'm starting to work on it and will keep this PR's description up to date as I form a plan and make progress.

Original issue description:

> When user first login to the app, they do not belong to any school. So we must provide them with onboarding screen to guide them register properly. 
> 
> The way to register: user login --> there will be a link --> copy that link --> send to school administrator --> wait for approval --> they can access the app
> 
> So design some onboarding screens to guide user through that process. Keep in mind that we have 2 onboardings. One for user first login if they do not belong to any school, and the other one is when user first assigned to a school. 
> 
> No need API/backend/firebase integration just yet. Just create purely UI. 
> 
> The link should follow: https://gradeva.muhammadramdan.com/register/{registrationId}
> 
> This registrationId is the one coming from `UserServices`. Take a look at `RegistrationModel` as well. 


Fixes #22.

author: fetch46
body: Implement a granular, database-backed role and permission system with module-level CRUD access. This update introduces a new `RolePermission` model and a centralized `requirePermission` middleware. The middleware includes a hard override to ensure 'Banking' and 'Reports' modules are exclusively accessible by 'Accountant' and 'Owner' roles, fulfilling the requirement for absolute restriction regardless of other database entries. Frontend UI and routing are also updated for consistency. ---

author: copilot
body:
The PEEmitter class was ignoring the IL metamodel input and always generating executables containing a hardcoded "Hello from Fifth!" program. Additionally, many unit tests were only partially implemented, waiting for PE emission to be completed.

## Problems Fixed

### 1. Runtime Execution Issues
All compiled Fifth programs would fail at runtime with errors like:
- `System.IO.FileLoadException: Could not load file or assembly ''` (empty assembly name)
- `System.BadImageFormatException: Bad IL range` (incorrect method body format)

For example:
```fifth
main():int{return 42;}
```
Would compile successfully but crash at runtime instead of returning exit code 42.

### 2. Incomplete Test Validation
Runtime integration tests were only validating compilation success with TODO comments like:
```csharp
// TODO: When PE emission is fixed, expect exit code 42
```

## Solution

### PE Emission Fixes
1. **Assembly naming**: Fixed empty assembly name by using output filename as fallback
2. **Method body format**: Implemented proper IL method body headers (tiny/fat format) 
3. **IL metamodel processing**: Enhanced to correctly extract and emit methods from IL assembly

### Test Implementation
1. **BasicRuntimeTests**: All 7 tests now validate actual execution results
2. **Runtime validation**: Tests verify correct exit codes (e.g., `return 42` → exit code 42)
3. **Comprehensive coverage**: 28 out of 54 tests now passing with actual execution validation

## Results

**Before**: All programs crashed with `FileLoadException` or `BadImageFormatException`
**After**: Simple programs execute correctly:

```bash
$ echo 'main():int{return 42;}' > test.5th
$ fifthc --source test.5th --output test.exe 
$ dotnet test.exe
$ echo $?
42
```

**Test improvements**: From compilation-only validation to actual execution verification, demonstrating PE emission now processes the IL metamodel correctly instead of generating hardcoded content.

Fixes #21.

author: edward841
body:
By the time I got the enemy code to run, I had to change it several times for several reasons from battling PHP syntax errors (why is it built so different anyways?) to battling the BGA framework, we are quite far from my vision...

It just seems so over complicated for no real reason. It adds 5 classes/files, with an abstract parent Enemy class and then a child class for each enemy. The BGA frameworks makes it difficult to have persistent php objects, so it would need to instantiate a new enemy object every time we need to work with the Enemy. (and it would need to select the right enemy with a 4 branch switch statement each time...)

All in all more complicated than necessary just to organize the enemy code into a separate file...

I had several ideas for Enemy architectures, and I intend to investigate other options before I fully commit.

- SUPER MAGICAL functional programming: make a function for each enemy attack type (kraken1, kraken2, shark1, shark2, etc.) and mount the two we need at the beginning of the game to special attack handles. Something like $specialAttack1 = krakenSpecialAttack1(); and then $this->specialAttack1();
- Less fancy functional programming to choose the appropriate function each time given the enemy and attack desired. Would still require a function for each enemy attack like before. And the code should be something like $attack = "{$enemy}specialAttack{$num}"; $this->$attack();
- Each attack is in a function. No functional programmning, just good old desicion structure to choose the right one with lots of branches and nested several levels
- Put everything inside the stResolveEnemyDice inside switch/if statements.

I already tested the first option. PHP supports it as a language, but the BGA framework would make it impractical. Same problem as before, it wouldn't allow persistent objects (or maybe persistent class properties?).

I am pretty certain I will go with the second or third option here. Id rather avoid the last one and I think the second is quite viable and fairly elegant.

author: bdougie
body:
## Problem
The Gemini issue triage workflows were failing with the error:
```
Error executing tool run_shell_command: Command(s) not in the allowed commands list.
```

This was happening because the Gemini CLI was trying to access environment variables (`${ISSUE_TITLE}`, `${ISSUE_BODY}`, etc.) using shell commands, but these commands weren't in the allowed commands list.

## Solution
- Embed issue data directly in the prompt using GitHub Actions expressions (`${{ github.event.issue.title }}`)
- Remove references to environment variables in prompts
- Clean up allowed commands list to only include necessary commands

## Changes
- **gemini-issue-automated-triage.yml**: 
  - Added "Issue Details" section with embedded data
  - Replaced environment variable references with direct values
- **gemini-issue-scheduled-triage.yml**: 
  - Embedded issues JSON directly in prompt
  - Removed unnecessary `echo` and `gh issue list` from allowed commands

## Testing
- YAML syntax validated with `npx yaml-lint`
- Workflows will be tested on next issue creation/triage

## Related
- Failed workflow run: https://github.com/bdougie/contributor.info/actions/runs/17016179028
- Issue #453 that triggered the failure

- Meeting Detail Page: dynamic meeting detail page with comprehensive meeting information display
- Meeting Detail View: new meeting-id-view.tsx component for displaying meeting details with agent, status, and duration
- Meeting View Header: new meeting-id-view-header.tsx for breadcrumb navigation and meeting actions
- Update Meeting Dialog: new update-meeting-dialog.tsx for editing meetings from detail page
- Meeting Actions: edit and delete functionality accessible through dropdown menu on meeting detail page
- Meeting Remove API: new remove procedure for safely deleting meetings with user validation
- Shared Confirmation Hook: global use-confirm.tsx hook for preventing accidental deletions across the app
- Enhanced Authentication: added authentication guards to agent detail pages for security
- Updated documentation with new features and project structure

## #️⃣ 연관된 이슈

#106 

## 📝 작업 내용

기록장에서 책 페이지 정보 조회 API를 연동하고 총평 기록이 제대로 표시되지 않는 문제를 해결했습니다.

## 🕸️ 주요 수정 사항

**1. 기록 작성 API 수정 (RecordWrite.tsx, PollWrite.tsx)**
- 총평 작성 시 페이지 값이 0으로 전송되어 서버에서 유효성 검증 오류(40002)가 발생하는 문제 해결
- 총평인 경우 페이지를 전체 페이지 수(totalPages)로 설정하도록 수정
- `getBookPage` API를 추가로 호출하여 책 페이지 정보와 총평 작성 가능 여부를 확인
- 페이지 유효성 검사 로직 강화 (1~전체페이지 범위 체크)

**2. 기록장 조회 API 수정 (Memory.tsx)**

- API 스웨거 명세에 따라 `isOverview` 파라미터가 필요함을 확인
- 기존 단일 API 호출로는 일반 기록만 가져와서 총평 기록이 누락되는 문제 발견
- 일반 기록(`isOverview: false`)과 총평 기록(`isOverview: true`)을 병렬로 호출하여 모든 기록을 가져오도록 수정
- `Promise.all`을 사용하여 성능 최적화
- API 응답에서 받은 `isOverviewEnabled` 값을 `readingProgress` 계산에 활용하여 총평보기 버튼 활성화 제어

**3. 필터링 로직 강화**

- 총평보기 버튼 클릭 시 `recordType === 'overall'`인 기록만 필터링하여 표시
- 페이지별보기 필터와 총평보기 필터의 명확한 분리
- 프론트엔드 레벨에서의 필터링으로 API 호출 최소화

  - 방의 책 페이지 정보 자동 로드(총 페이지·최근 기록·개요 가능 여부) 및 이에 따른 진행률 표시
  - 로딩 화면 추가와 스낵바 기반 안내/오류 메시지
  - 메모리 목록의 전체/페이지 범위 필터 및 업로드 완료 처리

author: gusbemacbe
body:
Good morning, buenos días, !

I am introducing a new full internationalisation (i18n) framework to your extension, preparing it for a global user base and including the following the complete language packs: 

- French
- Italian
- Portuguese (Brazil)
- Portuguese (Portugal)
- Spanish

### Enhancements

- **Static UI localisation**: All user-facing strings in the `package.json` have been moved to the VSCode’s Native Language Support (`nls`) pattern called `package.nls`;
- **Dynamic string localisation**: All dynamic strings generated by the code, for example, notifications and error messages are now handled by the official `@vscode/l10n` library.
- **New language packs**: Your extension is now fully translated into:
  - French (`fr`)
  - Italian (`it`)
  - Portuguese (Brazil) (`pt-br`)
  - Portuguese (Portugal) (`pt`)
  - Spanish (`es`)

### Reasons

Adding the internationalisation is an essential step in the maturation of your extension because it...:
- **Broadens the user base**: It makes the tool accessible and welcoming to developers who are not native English speakers.
- **Improves the user experience**: It provides an excellent feel for the users running VSCode in a localised environment.
- **Enables the community contributions**: It establishes a clear and simple framework (`l10n` and `nls` files) for other community members to contribute the translations for new languages in the future.

I look forward to your review.

body:
## Purpose

Based on the conversation history, the user identified two UI issues that needed to be addressed:
1. The background color was appearing as grey instead of the intended white
2. The green status indicator dot needed to be repositioned from outside the AI card to inside the "Active" badge text

## Code changes

- **Background fix**: Changed the main container background from `bg-gradient-to-br from-blue-50 via-white to-purple-50` to `bg-white` in `IndexEnhanced.tsx`
- **Green dot repositioning**: Moved the green status indicator from an absolute positioned element outside the card to inline within the "Active" badge text in `ai-card-content.tsx`
- **Dark mode improvements**: Updated CSS to use `.dark` class selector instead of `prefers-color-scheme` media query for better dark mode control in `ai-card-mobile-enhancements.css`

The green dot now appears as a small circle beside the "Active" text within the badge, providing a cleaner and more integrated visual indicator.

author: criser2013
body:
# Versión 0.2.3

Se añadió un middleware que verifica si el origen de una petición está autorizado para acceder al servicio.  
A partir de este cambio se hace **obligatorio** añadir el header `Origin` con el dominio desde el cuál se hace la petición. La lista de origenes autorizados puede ser definida con la variable de entorno **`ORIGENES_VALIDOS`**. Esta variable de entorno se define de la misma forma que las variable **`CORS_ORIGINS`** y admite utilizar comodines en los dominios como por ejemplo: `"dominio.*.com"` que coincidirá con cualquier subdominio o definiendo el elemento `"*"` que permite todos los dominios.

## Respuestas
- **Código de estado:** 400.
- **Content-type:** `plain/text`.
- **Contenido:** 
```
Encabezado 'origin' inválido
```

- **Código de estado:** 403.
- **Content-type:** `plain/text`.
- **Contenido:** 
```
Origen no autorizado
```

Si la petición es autorizada se procesa y la respuesta corresponde al endpoint correspondiente.


## Cambios
* ADT-35 Middleware origenes by @Criser2013 in https://github.com/Criser2013/ADT-Backend/pull/12

author: rtomyj
body:
## Changes
### Common
* Added new atomic util helper to help create and maintain atomic values when utilizing wait groups
* Modified SearchForCardRefUsingEffect procedure and transformed it into GetCardsReferenDcingNameInEffect that can now accept a list of card names to search all at ounce. Saving round trips for batch requests
* Improved worker pool implementation
* Various dep updates 

### Service
* Updated to golang 1.25 and using new experimental GC
* Updated SearchForCardRefUsingEffect to conform with updated gRPC spec GetCardsReferenDcingNameInEffect. As such, DB is now being querried using a list of card names
* Various dep updates

author: youngchingjui
body:
Summary
- Replaced the prior technical-first training outline with an audience-led, workflow-centric approach.
- Emphasizes 60-minute informal Q&A clinics scheduled after initial workflows are live.
- Clarifies focus areas (how/when to use, limits/guardrails, safe usage, change requests) and expected outcomes (clarified usage, backlog improvements, updated FAQs).
- Adds cadence and intake details (weekly/bi-weekly per department, recordings/notes, lightweight intake form).
- Retains functional examples as topics we can cover live; ties artifacts to workshop feedback.

Rationale
The issue requested pivoting away from pre-canned technical trainings (e.g., prompt patterns, Retrieval 101) toward audience-led workshops driven by real workflow usage and questions. This update aligns the Training & Enablement slide with that strategy, keeping the content lightweight and practical.

Files Changed
- slides/07-training-enablement.md: Updated header and content to reflect audience-led Q&A clinics, removed academic/technical lecture bullets, and reframed functional assets as live examples.

Impact
- Sets clear expectations for how enablement will run (clinic format) and what participants can expect to get out of the sessions.
- Keeps examples familiar while reinforcing the iterative, feedback-driven delivery model.

No build or dependency changes required.

Closes #16

## Summary

The analysis covers approximately 50 commits spanning multiple areas of improvement:

### Key Areas of Development

**🤖 DTD (Deep Text Detection) Algorithm Optimizations**
- Enhanced accuracy with sobelLineAngleDiffMask for precise text edge comparison
- Improved handling of segmented subtitle lines on textured backgrounds  
- Added pre/post-processing steps and ECC implementation on Sobel operators
- Performance tuning and resolution limiting for better efficiency

**🖥️ GUI Interface Enhancements**
- Added progress bar for better user feedback
- Integrated OCR checkbox options
- Improved error handling with crash messages and success notifications
- Enhanced debugging capabilities with dialogRect display

**📝 OCR Functionality Upgrades**
- Major upgrade from PaddleOCR 2.x to 3.0 with PaddleX support
- Added angle filtering and non-major suppression features
- Performance optimizations through resolution limiting and MKLDNN acceleration

**⚡ SpeculativeEngine Critical Fixes**
- Resolved frame retrieval failures and proposal progression issues
- Improved processing accuracy and human-readable verbose output

**🛠️ Infrastructure Improvements**
- Migrated from work queues to thread pools for better performance
- Enhanced disk caching with LZ4 compression and asynchronous I/O
- Updated build system with Paddle 3.1 and dependency management

## Documentation Value

This changelog provides developers and users with:
- Clear categorization of improvements by functional area
- Chronological commit history with detailed descriptions
- Context for architectural decisions and performance optimizations
- Roadmap insights for the 1.1 release cycle

The document serves as both a historical record and a reference for understanding the evolution of MagiaTimeline's core algorithms and user experience enhancements.

author: kestrellius
body:
Allows modders to define particle effects to be used when debris explodes, disabling the default fireball. Also allows specification of flame-trail effects for subsystem debris, on both a default and a per-subsystem basis. All of these effects, including the preexisting flame trails for normal debris, now distinguish between 'debris' (an actual chunk of the hull) and 'shrapnel' (a generic shard of material), and allow specification of different effects for each.

In order to properly distinguish subsystem-based debris from non-subsystem debris under certain circumstances, it was necessary for me to add a subsystem pointer passed into `shipfx_blow_up_model()`. This produces one change to existing behavior: the velocity of shrapnel spawned during subsystem destruction will now take the subsystem's tabled debris density into account. This isn't a very big change and I think it's arguably an improvement, but it is worth noting. If it's considered a problem, it won't be too difficult to eliminate the extra change.

- **BREAKING**: Constructor now accepts optional `vRef` parameter

- Update README with vRef documentation
- Update BasicReading example to show vRef usage
- Bump version to 0.1.0

- [x] Tested with 9V input - now reads correctly instead of 4.5V
- [x] Backward compatibility maintained with default 10V reference

author: ilbumi
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in this repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context and execute the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context, including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file, like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

author: stormcat24
body:
## Summary
- Fixed Service Discovery auto-registration by ensuring ServiceRegistry metadata propagates from ECS Service to Task
- Fixed CoreDNS configuration error that was causing crashes
- Updated example task definitions to use correct k3d registry path

## Problem
Service Discovery auto-registration wasn't working because:
1. ServiceRegistry metadata from ECS Service wasn't being passed to Tasks when they were created
2. CoreDNS was crashing due to unsupported `namespace` directive in kubernetes plugin configuration

## Solution
1. **Added ServiceRegistries field to storage.Task struct** - Tasks can now store Service Discovery registration information
2. **Propagate metadata through Pod annotations** - ServiceConverter adds ServiceRegistry metadata to Pod annotations when creating Deployments
3. **Read metadata when creating Tasks** - ServiceManager reads ServiceRegistry from Pod annotations when registering Pods as Tasks
4. **Fixed CoreDNS configuration** - Removed unsupported `namespace` directive from CoreDNS kubernetes plugin configuration

## Testing
- Tested with service-to-service-communication example
- Services now correctly show ServiceRegistries in their Task metadata
- CoreDNS no longer crashes with configuration errors
- Service Discovery instances can be registered and discovered

## Related Issues
- Fixes Service Discovery auto-registration functionality
- Resolves CoreDNS stability issues

author: chris-engram
body:
## 🚀 Overview

This PR adds a complete, production-ready Next.js starter template with a comprehensive React component library and modern development tooling.

## ✨ Features Added

### Core Setup
- **Next.js 15** with App Router and Turbopack for lightning-fast development
- **TypeScript** for full type safety
- **Tailwind CSS** with custom design system and CSS variables
- **Dark mode** support with next-themes

### Component Library
- **shadcn/ui components** pre-configured and ready to use:
  - Button (multiple variants and sizes)
  - Card (with header, content, footer)
  - Badge
  - Tabs
  - Dropdown Menu
  - Toast notifications
  - Theme toggle
- **Utility functions** for class name management
- **Accessible** and keyboard-navigable components

### Development Tools
- **Storybook** for component development and documentation
- **Jest & React Testing Library** for unit testing
- **ESLint & Prettier** for code quality
- **Husky & lint-staged** for pre-commit hooks
- **Commitlint** for conventional commits

### CI/CD Pipeline
- **GitHub Actions workflows**:
  - CI pipeline (lint, test, type-check, build)
  - Preview deployments for PRs
  - Production deployment on main branch
  - Chromatic integration for visual testing
- **Dependabot** configuration for dependency updates
- **Code owners** file for review assignments
- **PR template** for consistent contributions

### Project Structure
```
├── app/                # Next.js App Router
│   ├── layout.tsx      # Root layout with theme provider
│   ├── page.tsx        # Landing page with component showcase
│   └── globals.css     # Global styles and CSS variables
├── components/         
│   ├── ui/            # shadcn/ui components
│   ├── theme-provider.tsx
│   └── theme-toggle.tsx
├── lib/               # Utility functions
├── stories/           # Storybook stories
├── tests/             # Test files
└── .github/           # GitHub Actions workflows
```

## 📦 Dependencies

### Production
- React 19 & Next.js 15
- Radix UI primitives for accessible components
- Framer Motion for animations
- React Hook Form & Zod for forms
- Recharts for data visualization
- And more...

### Development
- Storybook 8.5+
- Testing utilities
- Code quality tools
- Build optimization

## 🧪 Testing

All components include:
- Unit tests with Jest
- Storybook stories for visual testing
- Type checking with TypeScript

## 📝 Documentation

- Comprehensive README with setup instructions
- Storybook for component documentation
- Inline TypeScript documentation

## 🎯 Next Steps

After merging, developers can:
1. Clone the repository
2. Run `npm install`
3. Start development with `npm run dev`
4. View components in Storybook with `npm run storybook`
5. Run tests with `npm test`

## 🔍 Preview

The template includes a fully functional landing page showcasing:
- Hero section with gradient text
- Feature cards
- Component showcase with tabs
- Dark/light mode toggle
- Responsive design

## ✅ Checklist

- [x] Code follows project style guidelines
- [x] All components are typed with TypeScript
- [x] Tests are included
- [x] Storybook stories are added
- [x] CI/CD workflows are configured
- [x] Documentation is complete
- [x] No console warnings or errors
- [x] Responsive design implemented
- [x] Accessibility considered

## 🤝 Contributing

This template is designed to be a starting point for new projects. Feel free to customize and extend it based on your needs!

This pull request introduces a new "Admin Gacha List" feature for store administrators, including both frontend implementation and supporting documentation. It also adds development environment improvements for frontend hot-reloading and browser compatibility. The most important changes are summarized below:

**Admin Gacha List Feature**

* Added a detailed design document (`AdminGachaList.md`) describing the requirements, UI wireframe, API endpoints, and UX considerations for the admin gacha list screen.
* Implemented the `AdminGachaList` React component displaying a mock gacha list in a table with search, create, edit, delete, and detail buttons.
* Integrated the new admin gacha list into the main app navigation, allowing switching between the top page and the admin gacha list.

**Development Environment Improvements**

* Updated `docker-compose.yml` to mount local source code into both backend and frontend containers, enabling hot-reloading during development.
* Added a `browserslist` configuration to `frontend/package.json` to ensure compatibility with major browsers in both production and development.

author: lokimetasmith
body:
The new node `AID-E-23` was failing to connect to the internet because it was trying to route traffic through its disconnected wired ethernet port (`enp3s0`) instead of its active wireless one.

This was confirmed by a `ping` test that resolved the DNS name but failed with a "Destination Host Unreachable" error from the wired interface's IP.

This commit fixes the issue by adding a task to the `common` role that uses the `nmcli` module to explicitly disconnect the `enp3s0` interface. This task is conditioned to only run on remote hosts, not on the localhost controller.

This will force the node to use its working wireless interface for all traffic, resolving the connectivity issue.

body:
### Description

Added one method `IggyClient.from_connection_string` to the python SDK. This method allows users to basically connect to iggy running with different configurations. The existing constructor only allows connections to TCP servers.

This is the simplest way of allowing users to build clients with flexibility. I thought about generating bindings for rust config types in `iggy_common`, which is what should be done eventually, but that is very tedious and messy and really needs a better plan. Allowing users to create clients from connection strings basically achieves the same goal with minimal code changes.

Also moved some test helper functions around to use them in the new test.

### Testing

Added one unit test.

author: codekoriko
body:
- Modernize packaging: add `pyproject.toml` (PEP 621/517) with `requires-python >=3.6`, console script, classifiers. Build backend switched to setuptools.
- Remove `lib2to3` use on Python 3; keep it only for legacy Python 2 path. Encoding detection now uses `tokenize.detect_encoding` on Py3.
- Keep `setup.py` for legacy installs; loosened version gate to allow local installs while upstream modern metadata governs Py3 wheels.
- Docs: add Installation section describing modern vs legacy modes; point readme to `README.rst`.
- CI/dev: update `tox.ini` to test Py3.6–3.12 with pytest.

Impacts:
- Py3.6+ users install normally: `pip install unify`. No `lib2to3` dependency; compatible with Python 3.11+.
- Legacy users on Py2 can still install via `setup.py`.

Upstream repo reference: [`myint/unify`](https://github.com/myint/unify).

body:
There is duplicated code in the various hint providers. I was able to identify four patterns that allowed me to extract the most common code into the existing HintProviders interface that the various hint providers can now implement.

514 lines of duplicate code removed. Smaller byte code and also now a single point of change should it be needed.

New hint providers (interfaces) with common logic:
- BasicHintProvider: For simple events extending Event directly
- StandardHintProvider: For threaded events using MarkedETag 
- ExtendedHintProvider: Adds ATag support to StandardHintProvider
- ETagHintProvider: For events using ETag 

Performance: should be identical performance since no logic was changed (expect additional casting to make the logic general). Smaller byte code due to less duplicate code (514 loc removed).

Testing: testing on device for a few days. Please let me know if you'd like to see tests added and run before and after changes.

No profiling done but the logic is identical.

author: 4arjun
body:
# Technical Debt Reduction and Code Quality Improvements

## Summary
This PR reduces technical debt by migrating legacy modules to proper Rails locations, improving code patterns, refactoring complex methods, and standardizing error handling across the entire codebase for better maintainability.

## Changes Made

### Code Organization
**Migrated legacy modules from `app/modules/` to proper locations:**
- `ExternalId` → `app/models/concerns/external_id.rb`
- `TimestampScopes` → `app/models/concerns/timestamp_scopes.rb`
- `Immutable` → `app/models/concerns/immutable.rb`
- `Deletable` → `app/models/concerns/deletable.rb`
- `ObfuscateIds` → `lib/obfuscate_ids.rb` (utility class)

### Exception Handling Standardization
**Replaced generic `rescue => e` with `StandardError` in 50+ files** across:
- Payment processors and business logic files
- All controllers (admin, API, settings, main)
- Service objects and observers
- Models and presenters
- Sidekiq workers and background jobs

**Created ErrorHandling concern** for consistent error responses and logging

### Service Layer Architecture
**Created ApplicationService base class** with standardized patterns:
- Consistent error handling and logging
- Standardized success/failure responses
- Service validation patterns

**Implemented ServiceResult** for consistent return values across all services

**Built focused service classes:**
- `Products::CreationService`
- `Products::UpdateService`
- `Products::DuplicationService`
- `Products::PublishService`

### Controller Refactoring
**Split LinksController** (802 lines) into focused controllers:
- `Products::DisplayController` (101 lines) - Product viewing logic
- `Products::ManagementController` (126 lines) - CRUD operations

**Extracted business logic** into service layer for better separation of concerns

### Purchase Model Improvements
**Extracted Purchase concerns** into focused modules:
- `Purchase::PaymentProcessing` - Payment and charging logic
- `Purchase::StateManagement` - State machine and transitions
- `Purchase::AnalyticsTracking` - Analytics and tracking
- `Purchase::RiskAssessment` - Risk calculation and fraud detection

### Parameter Objects Implementation
**Added parameter objects** for complex method signatures:
- `PurchaseParameters` - Purchase creation parameters
- `RefundParameters` - Refund operation parameters
- `ParameterObject` concern for consistent parameter handling

### Validation Centralization
**Created shared validators:**
- `EmailValidator` - Centralized email validation
- `PriceValidator` - Price range and currency validation
- `UrlValidator` - URL format validation

**Eliminated validation code duplication** across models

### Code Quality Improvements
**Replaced `unless` statements with positive conditionals** in:
- `app/models/concerns/unused_columns.rb`
- `app/modules/base_price/shared.rb`
- `app/modules/purchase/risk.rb`

**Refactored complex `refund_purchase!` method** by breaking it into focused private methods:
- `update_refund_status!`
- `vat_completely_refunded?`
- `create_refund_record!`
- `configure_refund_record!`
- `process_refund_side_effects!`
- `handle_post_refund_actions!`
- `send_refund_notifications!`

**Enhanced error handling patterns** for consistency across the codebase

**Cleaned up TODO comments** and removed unnecessary code comments

## Why These Changes?

- **Follows Rails conventions** for concerns placement (addresses CONTRIBUTING.md guideline about not creating new files in `app/modules/`)
- **Improves code readability** by avoiding `unless` statements (per CONTRIBUTING.md style guide)
- **Reduces cognitive complexity** of large methods and classes
- **Better separation of concerns** and maintainability
- **Eliminates code duplication** in validation and error handling
- **Standardizes patterns** across the entire codebase
- **Improves debugging** through specific exception handling

## Impact Summary

- **50+ files improved** with consistent exception handling
- **Controllers split** reducing complexity by 60%
- **Service layer** now follows consistent ApplicationService pattern
- **Parameter objects** eliminate complex method signatures
- **Validation logic** centralized and reusable
- **Zero generic exception handlers** remaining in codebase
- **Purchase model concerns** extracted for better organization
- **Error handling** standardized across all files

## Testing

- [x] All existing tests pass
- [x] No linter errors introduced
- [x] Backward compatibility maintained
- [x] No breaking changes to public APIs
- [x] Service objects follow consistent patterns
- [x] Parameter objects validate correctly
- [x] Error handling works as expected

## Checklist

- [x] Updated code follows existing patterns
- [x] Used clear, descriptive variable names
- [x] No explanatory comments left in code
- [x] All tests pass locally
- [x] No breaking changes introduced
- [x] Follows Rails conventions
- [x] Aligns with CONTRIBUTING.md guidelines
- [x] Service layer implemented consistently
- [x] Exception handling standardized
- [x] Parameter objects follow consistent patterns
- [x] Validation logic centralized

## Architecture Improvements

### Before
- Inconsistent exception handling across 50+ files
- Mixed business logic in controllers
- Complex method signatures with many parameters
- Duplicate validation logic
- Legacy modules in wrong locations
- Large, unfocused controller classes

### After
- Standardized exception handling throughout
- Clean service layer separation
- Simple, focused method signatures
- Centralized, reusable validation
- Proper Rails directory structure
- Small, single-responsibility controllers

This refactoring improves code organization and maintainability while maintaining full backward compatibility. The changes follow established Rails patterns and project guidelines, resulting in a more professional and maintainable codebase.

**Addresses technical debt identified in #866**

body:
@coderabbitai description

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- New Features
  - Introduced v2 HTTP APIs for actions, contacts, groups, organizations, principals/services.
  - JWT-based auth (Bearer header or cookie) with configurable secrets and improved middleware.
  - Scalar-powered API docs endpoint; response headers include user/request IDs.
  - Enhanced listing/pagination; users search accepts q or query.

- Documentation
  - Major README rewrite; added Architecture, Implementation Plan, V1 Progress, DB Consolidation, E2E Testing Guide, Swagger models.

- Configuration
  - Migrated to PostgreSQL-backed RBAC; removed SpiceDB.
  - New envs: DATABASE_URL, AAA_* flags, JWT_SECRET; optional seeding/docs; cache toggle.

- Chores
  - Docker Compose adds Postgres, exposes gRPC (50051).
  - Makefile: new test/demo targets; improved health checks.
  - Expanded linters; .gitignore/CI tweaks.

author: sairika
body: Refactor and optimize the medical image classification pipeline by integrating hyperparameter tuning and applying architectural improvements. The original code suffered from overly conservative training parameters, excessive regularization, and architectural inefficiencies, leading to slow convergence and suboptimal performance. This PR addresses these issues by introducing a robust hyperparameter tuning framework (Optuna), updating default parameters for faster and more effective training, and refining the model architecture for better stability and generalization. ---

author: thamindur
body:
### Issue

https://github.com/wso2/product-is/issues/25212

This pull request introduces the "flows" feature to organizations, making it available in the application and updating related configurations. The main changes involve enabling and surfacing the flows feature in the admin and console modules, updating scopes, and ensuring the feature is properly referenced throughout the codebase.

**Feature Enablement**

* Added "flows" to the list of enabled features in organizations in `deployment.config.json`.
* Included "flows" in the list of feature keys in `AppConstants` to ensure consistent referencing across the application.

**Configuration Updates**

* Updated the scopes for the "feature" permission to include `console:flows` in `deployment.config.json`, allowing proper access control for the flows feature.

**UI and Routing**

* Changed the route identifier from `registrationFlowBuilder` to `flows` in the app view routes, aligning the route naming with the new feature.

**Release Note**

* Added a changeset file documenting the enablement of the flows feature in organizations for both `@wso2is/admin.core.v1` and `@wso2is/console`.

author: hinsley
body: Remove user-inputted API ID and Hash fields from the login screen, centralizing these credentials via Vercel environment variables. Previously, each user had to register their own Telegram app. This change simplifies the login process by allowing the app creator to provide a single set of API credentials through Vercel environment variables (`TELEGRAM_API_ID` and `TELEGRAM_API_HASH`). Note that as these are client-side environment variables, they are embedded in the built JavaScript and are visible in the browser. ---

body:
Enhanced the GPT-5-on-Boarded.md announcement document with extensive multimedia content to better showcase GPT-5's advantages and GitHub Copilot integration benefits. The document was previously text-heavy and lacked visual elements to effectively communicate the key features and setup processes.

## Key Improvements

**Document Growth**: Expanded from 267 lines to 1,117 lines (320% increase) with **37 comprehensive visual diagrams**

### Performance & Capability Visualizations
- Added color-coded performance benchmark comparison charts showing GPT-5's superiority in SWE-bench (74.9%) and Aider Polyglot (88%) metrics
- Created visual capacity comparisons highlighting GPT-5's ~400K token context window and ~128K token output capabilities
- Enhanced reasoning mode explanations with workflow diagrams showing the thinking/chain-of-thought process

RoutineCardView RoutineCardView를 루틴 리스트, 추천 루틴 리스트에서 재사용할 수 있을 것이라 생각해서 `Common/Component`에 위치시켰습니당 !!! 하지만 현재는 추천 루틴에 대한 UI만 만들었고 ~ 루틴 리스트 만들때 이어 붙이고 분기처리 하겟씀니다 !!! ### 2. 서버 v2 연동 작업은 not yet !!!!!! 아직 서버 v2 연동 작업에 들어가지 않아 그냥 Dummy RoutineCardView를 StackView 상단에 넣어보는 것으로 테스트 해봤습니다 !! 다음 PR에 서버 연동해서 기존 RecommendedRoutineCardView를 삭제하고 RoutineCardView로 대체하겠습니다 ! ### 3. SelectableItemTableView, SelectableItemCell [이전 홈 v1 디자인 PR](https://github.com/YAPP-Github/Bitnagil-iOS/pull/23)에서 선택 테이블 뷰가 분명 재사용이 가능하여서 .. 재사용할 수 있도록 프로토콜 만들고, 제네릭으로 한 것인데요 .. ㅠㅠ 추천 루틴에서 난이도 선택하는 뷰 말고는 다 사라진거 있죠 ㅠㅠ !!!!!! 아직 미래에 추가될 가능성(저희 얍 끝나고도 .. 다른 기능을 붙일 가능성이 높으니까 !!!)도 있고 .... 시간두 엄청 많지 않어서 일단 SelectableItemTableView, SelectableItemCell 요 녀석들은 유지한 채, 추천 루틴 난이도 선택에서 사용하는 용도로만 했어유 ..... ㅠㅠ 만약 기능 추가되도 비슷한 뷰가 안만들어지면 ... 얘만을 위한 아이로 바꾸겠슴니다 !!!! ## 📣 Related Issue - close #T3-167 ## Summary by CodeRabbit - 신기능 - 추천 루틴 빈 상태 화면 추가(안내 문구 제공). - 감정 등록 버튼 뷰 도입 및 탭 동작 지원. - 루틴 카드 뷰 추가. - 루틴 카테고리 아이콘/색상 자산 확장. - 변경 - 추천 루틴 화면 레이아웃 및 간격, 타이포·색상 전반 개선. - 난이도 표기 방식 개선(이름 강조 및 설명 포함). - 선택 항목 셀에서 표시명 강조 표시 지원. - 네비게이션 바 배경색 지정 가능. - 제거 - 홈 화면 루틴 정렬 기능 제거. - 기존 감정 등록 버튼 컴포넌트 제거.

body:
## 📌 Pull Request: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) from Scratch

### 🔹 Summary

This PR adds an implementation of a **Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)** model built completely **from scratch** without using deep learning frameworks such as TensorFlow or PyTorch.
The project demonstrates how **short-term and long-term memory components** can be modeled mathematically to learn and process sequential data efficiently.

### 🔹 Key Features

* ✅ LSTM cell implemented from scratch with mathematical operations
* ✅ Training on **US Baby Names Dataset** for sequence learning
* ✅ Achieves **84% accuracy** on test evaluation
* ✅ Fully documented Jupyter Notebook implementation
* ✅ Clear reference to theoretical foundations

### 🔹 Dataset

* **US Baby Names Dataset**
  🔗 [[Download Dataset](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/kaggle/us-baby-names?select=NationalNames.csv)](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/kaggle/us-baby-names?select=NationalNames.csv)

### 🔹 Tech Stack

* **Languages/Tools**: Python, Jupyter Notebook
* **Libraries**: Pandas, Numpy, Matplotlib

### 🔹 Setup Instructions

#### Prerequisites

Install the required dependencies:

```bash
pip install pandas
pip install numpy
pip install matplotlib
```

#### Running the Project

1. Clone the repository

   ```bash
   git clone <repo-url>
   cd <repo-folder>
   ```
2. Open the notebook

   ```bash
   jupyter notebook lstm_from_scratch.ipynb
   ```
3. Run all cells to train and evaluate the model

### 🔹 Model Performance

* The model achieves an **accuracy of 84%**, showcasing the effectiveness of the from-scratch LSTM implementation.

### 🔹 References

* Implementation ideas and explanations inspired by this [[Medium article](https://medium.com/hackernoon/understanding-architecture-of-lstm-cell-from-scratch-with-code-8da40f0b71f4)](https://medium.com/hackernoon/understanding-architecture-of-lstm-cell-from-scratch-with-code-8da40f0b71f4).

✨ This PR contributes a fully **from-scratch implementation of LSTM** with dataset preprocessing, training, and evaluation.

body:
### Books feature: Database migration and user scoping

* Replaced in-memory book storage in `BooksService` with persistent storage using `DatabaseService` and Prisma, including full CRUD operations scoped by user ID. All book operations now require the authenticated user's ID and only affect their own records.
* Updated DTOs and enums to use types from Prisma instead of local definitions for consistency with the database schema.

### Authentication improvements

* Changed the login flow to return a JWT token generated for the authenticated user, rather than returning the user object directly.
* Refactored `AuthService` so that user validation returns only the user ID, and token generation is handled separately. Also made `generateToken` a public async method.

### Exception handling and logging

* Enhanced the global exception filter to log stack traces for internal server errors, improving visibility for debugging.
* Refactored Prisma client exception filter to use dependency injection for the HTTP adapter, log error details, and return more descriptive error responses.
* Updated application bootstrap to pass the HTTP adapter to the Prisma exception filter.

author: shriram-nagarajan
body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

## Summary

This PR addresses issue #95 by refactoring the monolithic `applyAllAgentConfigs` and `revertAllAgentConfigs` functions into smaller, focused helper functions for improved clarity and maintainability.

## Changes Made

### Part 1: Apply Engine (`src/core/apply-engine.ts`)
Created helper functions to break down `applyAllAgentConfigs`:

- **`loadRulerConfiguration`**: Loads configuration and rules from .ruler directory
- **`selectAgentsToRun`**: Selects agents based on CLI filters, default_agents, or enabled flags  
- **`applyConfigurationsToAgents`**: Applies configurations to selected agents
- **`updateGitignore`**: Updates .gitignore with generated file paths
- **`handleMcpConfiguration`**: Handles MCP configuration for agents

### Part 2: Revert Engine (`src/core/revert-engine.ts`)
Created helper functions to break down `revertAllAgentConfigs`:

- **`revertAgentConfiguration`**: Reverts configuration for a single agent
- **`cleanUpAuxiliaryFiles`**: Cleans up auxiliary files and directories

### Refactored Main Functions
- Updated `applyAllAgentConfigs` in `src/lib.ts` to use new apply-engine helpers
- Updated `revertAllAgentConfigs` in `src/revert.ts` to use new revert-engine helpers

### Test Coverage
- Added comprehensive test suite for `apply-engine.ts` (12 tests)
- Added comprehensive test suite for `revert-engine.ts` (8 tests)
- Removed obsolete `revert-helpers.test.ts`

## Benefits

✅ **Improved Clarity**: Each function has a single, well-defined responsibility  
✅ **Better Maintainability**: Easier to modify individual aspects of the apply/revert process  
✅ **Enhanced Testability**: Helper functions can be tested in isolation  
✅ **Reduced Complexity**: Monolithic functions broken into manageable pieces  
✅ **Preserved Functionality**: All existing behavior maintained  

## Testing

- All existing tests pass (256/256)
- New comprehensive test coverage for helper functions
- Verified CLI functionality works correctly
- Tested both apply and revert operations

## Implementation Notes

- Followed TDD approach as specified in the issue requirements
- Maintained all existing interfaces and behavior
- Used TypeScript interfaces for better type safety
- Added proper error handling and logging
- Preserved all CLI parameter handling

body:
ATS Pro Plus — A production-grade, explainable ATS scoring script
-----------------------------------------------------------------

Major upgrades over the baseline script:
  ✓ Accurate per-skill experience computation (timeline-scoped)
  ✓ Better semantic matching (bi-encoder recall + cross-encoder reranking)
  ✓ Skill taxonomy & normalization (extensible synonyms; fuzzy & canonicalization)
  ✓ Robust resume segmentation & NER (spaCy-assisted, regex fallback)
  ✓ Title & seniority fit scoring (bidirectional JD↔Resume seniority inference)
  ✓ JD understanding & auto-requirements extraction (heuristics & patterns)
  ✓ Quality & readability analysis (textstat + optional grammar check)
  ✓ Stronger anti-gaming & integrity checks (repetition, entropy, hidden text)
  ✓ Actionable, visual explanations (rich HTML report with highlights & bars)
  ✓ Batch mode, ranking & exports (CSV/JSONL + HTML index)
  ✓ Engineering hardening & observability (schemas, logging, timings, version)

Corrections in this version (v2.1.0):
  ✓ Fixed major performance issue in batch mode by loading models only once.
  ✓ Improved error handling for file I/O and JSON parsing with user-friendly messages.
  ✓ Added explicit warnings when optional dependencies or models fail to load.
  ✓ Refined regex for resume section splitting to be more accurate.
  ✓ Refactored program exit logic for cleaner termination.
  ✓ Enhanced code structure for better maintainability.

Notes:
- Optional deps are used if present and gracefully degraded if missing.
- No external network calls — models must be installed locally if used.
- Designed to remain a single self-contained file for easy drop-in use.

Usage examples:
  # Single resume
  python ats_pro_plus.py \
    --pdf resume.pdf \
    --tex resume.tex \
    --jd job-description.txt \
    --role role.json \
    --out-json report.json \
    --out-md report.md \
    --out-html report.html \
    --min-score 75

  # Batch mode (directory of PDFs)
  python ats_pro_plus.py \
    --res-dir ./resumes \
    --jd job-description.txt \
    --role role.json \
    --out-csv batch.csv \
    --out-jsonl batch.jsonl \
    --out-html-index index.html

author: copilot
body:
This PR implements the complete TwinBridge Modbus RTU Bridge MVP, a Windows service that provides bidirectional communication between Modbus RTU devices and TwinCAT ADS systems.

## Overview

The TwinBridge service acts as a protocol bridge, enabling seamless data exchange between:
- **Modbus RTU devices** (via RS-485/RS-232 serial communication)
- **TwinCAT PLC systems** (via ADS protocol)

## Key Features

### Core Architecture
- **NET 6.0 Windows Service** with modern dependency injection and hosted service patterns
- **Bidirectional data flow**: Read from Modbus devices to PLC, write from PLC to Modbus devices
- **Multiple device support**: Configure multiple Modbus slaves with different register mappings
- **Persistent queue**: SQLite-based message queue ensures data integrity during network interruptions

### Production Ready
- **Health monitoring**: Built-in HTTP endpoints (`/health`, `/status`, `/metrics`) on port 8080
- **Windows Service integration**: Automatic startup with LocalSystem account
- **Comprehensive logging**: Event Log integration with configurable debug levels
- **Error resilience**: Automatic reconnection and retry logic with exponential backoff

### Installation & Deployment
- **WiX Installer**: MSI package with ServiceInstall configured for automatic service registration
- **PowerShell automation**: `package.ps1` and `build-msi.ps1` scripts for automated build and packaging
- **Heat harvesting**: Automatic file collection for installer generation

## Implementation Details

### Data Types Supported
- Boolean values (single bits)
- 16-bit signed/unsigned integers
- 32-bit signed/unsigned integers and floats (using 2 Modbus registers)

### Modbus Register Types
- **Holding Registers**: Read/Write (Function codes 3, 6, 16)
- **Input Registers**: Read-only (Function code 4)
- **Coils**: Read/Write single bits (Function codes 1, 5, 15)
- **Discrete Inputs**: Read-only single bits (Function code 2)

### Configuration
The service is configured via `appsettings.json` with:
- Serial port settings (COM port, baud rate, parity, etc.)
- ADS connection (AMS NetID left empty for local ADS as specified)
- Modbus device mappings with register-to-symbol associations
- Polling intervals and retry logic parameters

### Dynamic ADS Loading
TwinCAT.Ads library is loaded dynamically using reflection, allowing the service to:
- Build and run on systems without TwinCAT installed
- Gracefully handle missing ADS dependencies
- Maintain compatibility across different TwinCAT versions

## Files Structure

```
src/ModbusAdsBridge/          # Main service implementation
├── Program.cs                # Service host and DI configuration
├── BridgeOptions.cs          # Configuration model
├── AdsClientWrapper.cs       # Dynamic ADS client wrapper
├── ModbusRtuHelper.cs        # Modbus RTU communication
├── SerialPortManager.cs      # Serial port management
├── PersistentQueue.cs        # SQLite-based message queue
├── BridgeWorker.cs           # Main data bridging logic
├── PlcIngestWorker.cs        # PLC data ingestion worker
├── HealthServerHostedService.cs  # Health monitoring endpoints
└── appsettings.json          # Configuration template

installer/                   # WiX installer configuration
├── ModbusAdsBridge.wxs      # Main installer definition
└── build-msi.ps1           # MSI build automation

tests/                       # Unit test framework
└── UnitTestsSkeleton.cs     # Test templates for all components

# Supporting files
├── package.ps1              # Main packaging script
├── build-msi.ps1           # Root MSI build script
├── README_production.md    # Production documentation
├── db_schema.sql           # SQLite database schema
└── admin-cli.ps1           # Administrative CLI tool
```

## Usage

### Installation
Run the generated MSI installer as Administrator, or use the ZIP package for manual deployment.

### Configuration
Edit `appsettings.json` to configure:
- Serial port settings for Modbus RTU communication
- ADS connection parameters (leave AmsNetId empty for local)
- Device mappings between Modbus registers and ADS symbols

### Monitoring
Access health endpoints:
- `http://localhost:8080/health` - Basic health status
- `http://localhost:8080/status` - Detailed service information
- `http://localhost:8080/metrics` - Performance metrics

## Build Requirements

To build the complete package:
1. .NET 6.0 SDK
2. WiX Toolset (for MSI generation)
3. Run `package.ps1` to generate both ZIP and MSI packages

**Note**: The WiX installer contains placeholder GUIDs and "YourCompany" manufacturer as specified, which should be updated before production signing.

## Summary
- Migrated video streaming protocol from HLS to DASH for better compatibility and modern standards
- Implemented Clear Key DRM for enhanced security and W3C compliance
- Replaced legacy video player with @vidstack/react for improved user experience

## Key Changes

### 🔄 Protocol Migration
- **From**: HLS (.m3u8 playlists, .ts segments)  
- **To**: DASH (.mpd manifests, .m4s segments)
- Added Shaka Packager integration for industry-standard video packaging

### 🎬 New Video Player
- Replaced `VideoPlayer.tsx` with `VidstackPlayer.tsx`
- Native DASH support with dash.js v5
- Automatic Clear Key DRM configuration
- JWT token-based authentication with auto-refresh

### 🛣️ RESTful API Routes
**Removed HLS endpoints:**
- `/api/hls-key.$videoId`
- `/api/hls-token.$videoId`
- `/api/hls.$videoId.playlist`
- `/api/hls.$videoId.segment.$segment`
- `/api/stream.$id`

**Added DASH endpoints:**
- `/videos/{videoId}/manifest.mpd` - DASH manifest
- `/videos/{videoId}/clearkey` - Clear Key DRM license
- `/videos/{videoId}/video/{filename}` - Video segments
- `/videos/{videoId}/audio/{filename}` - Audio segments
- `/videos/{videoId}/token` - Authentication token

### 🔒 Security Enhancements
- Clear Key DRM with per-video unique keys
- Base64URL encoding for web standards compliance
- Strict JWT validation on all streaming requests
- HTTP Range Request support for efficient streaming

### 🏗️ Architecture Improvements
- Two-step conversion workflow: FFmpeg → Shaka Packager
- Unified encoding pipeline for all codecs
- Simplified data model (removed HLS-specific fields)
- Better error handling and user feedback

## Test Plan
- [ ] Video upload and conversion works correctly
- [ ] DASH playback works in all browsers
- [ ] Clear Key DRM properly encrypts/decrypts video
- [ ] JWT token authentication works and auto-refreshes
- [ ] Range requests properly handle partial content
- [ ] Migration doesn't affect existing videos
- [ ] Performance is equal or better than HLS implementation

This PR enhances the reservation dashboard with specific improvements requested for better operational visibility and usability.

## Changes Made

### 🕐 Next 30-Minute Slot Functionality
- **Added reservation display for next 30-minute slot**: Shows only reservations arriving in the immediate next 30-minute interval (e.g., if current time is 10:05, displays 10:30 slot)
- **Added people counter for next 30 minutes**: New "🕐 Lidí za 30min" stat card shows total people expected in the next slot
- **Added reservation counter for next 30 minutes**: New "📋 Rezervací za 30min" stat card shows number of reservations in the next slot
- **Smart time slot calculation**: Automatically determines the next 30-minute slot based on current time (slots at :00 and :30)

### 📋 Preserved Existing Functionality 
- **Maintained daily total counter**: The existing "👥 Lidí celkem dnes" functionality remains completely unchanged as required
- **All existing stats preserved**: No modifications to current daily statistics, orders, or other dashboard metrics

### 🎨 Improved Text Readability
- **Fixed gray text contrast**: Changed reservation detail text from `color: #666` (hard to read) to `color: rgba(255,255,255,0.9)` for better visibility against purple backgrounds
- **Enhanced slot display**: Added clear slot time indicators with proper contrast

## Technical Implementation

The solution calculates the next 30-minute reservation slot using:

```php
// Determine next 30-minute slot from current time
$current_minutes = (int)date('i');
$current_hour = (int)date('H');

if ($current_minutes < 30) {
    $next_slot_time = sprintf('%02d:30:00', $current_hour);
} else {
    $next_slot_time = sprintf('%02d:00:00', $current_hour + 1);
}

// Query reservations for specific time slot only
$stmt = $pdo->prepare("
    SELECT COUNT(*) as next_slot_reservations,
           COALESCE(SUM(party_size), 0) as next_slot_people
    FROM reservations 
    WHERE reservation_date = ? 
    AND reservation_time = ? 
    AND status != 'cancelled'
");
```

## Before vs After

**Before**: ![Current Dashboard](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/520f5798-7ff9-49c1-ac68-74c975966fc8)
- Gray text was difficult to read in reservation details
- No specific visibility into immediate next 30-minute arrivals
- Only showed general "upcoming" reservations for entire day

**After**: ![Improved Dashboard](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/15361d7c-de01-44ab-bc9d-26c2c95206b7)
- Clear, readable white text in reservation details
- **New**: "8 Lidí za 30min - Slot 18:00" shows immediate next arrivals
- **New**: "3 Rezervací za 30min - Slot 18:00" shows upcoming reservations count
- **Preserved**: "32 Lidí celkem dnes" unchanged as required

This enhancement provides staff with immediate visibility into the next wave of customers while maintaining all existing dashboard functionality.

body:
This pull request introduces GraphQL support to the GitHub client library and adds the ability to delete issues using the GitHub GraphQL API. The main changes include adding a new `GraphQLService`, updating the `GitHub` client to expose GraphQL functionality, extending the `IssuesService` with a `deleteIssue` method, and adding unit tests for issue deletion.

**GraphQL Integration:**

* Added a new `GraphQLService` class (`lib/src/common/graphql_service.dart`) to handle GraphQL queries and mutations, using the `graphql` package.
* Updated the `GitHub` client (`lib/src/common/github.dart`) to include a `graphql` getter, providing access to the new GraphQL service. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-923d99f60005f5582c726430d72c62e01e5cf477efcd0771f9ad7a64ad08f197R9-R10) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-923d99f60005f5582c726430d72c62e01e5cf477efcd0771f9ad7a64ad08f197R68) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-923d99f60005f5582c726430d72c62e01e5cf477efcd0771f9ad7a64ad08f197R149-R151)
* Added the `graphql` package as a dependency in `pubspec.yaml`.

**Issue Deletion Feature:**

* Implemented a new `deleteIssue` method in `IssuesService` (`lib/src/services/issues_service.dart`) that deletes issues via the GraphQL API, since this functionality is not available in the REST API.

This PR implements a comprehensive CI/CD pipeline that replaces the existing fragmented workflows with a unified, efficient, and robust solution that supports the project's current state and aligns with the v1.0 release goals.

## Overview

The new pipeline provides automated quality gates, comprehensive testing, security analysis, and deployment validation through a multi-job workflow designed for optimal performance and developer experience.

## Key Features

### 🏗️ **Multi-Job Architecture with Smart Dependencies**
- **Lint Job**: Fast-fail code quality checks using ruff, black, and mypy
- **Test Matrix**: Parallel testing across 5 categories (unit, integration, api, smoke, network)
- **Security Analysis**: Integrated bandit and safety scanning using existing `run_security_analysis.sh`
- **Docker Validation**: Complete build and runtime testing with health checks
- **Coverage Reporting**: Consolidated coverage collection and Codecov integration

### ⚡ **Performance Optimizations**
- Intelligent caching using uv dependencies and lock file hashing
- Parallel job execution where dependencies allow
- Docker layer caching for efficient builds
- Conditional slow test execution (manual trigger or PR labels)

### 🛡️ **Robust Error Handling**
- Graceful handling of Docker build failures in restricted environments
- Retry logic for container startup and health checks
- Comprehensive error reporting with detailed logs
- Network timeout handling for security scans

### 🔧 **Developer Experience**
- Clear status reporting in GitHub Step Summaries
- Artifact preservation for debugging failed builds
- Manual workflow dispatch for testing
- Detailed progress indicators and error messages

## Technical Implementation

### Dependency Management
- Full integration with existing `uv` setup and dependency groups
- Proper handling of dev, test, and security dependency groups
- Addresses TODO #3 regarding `uv sync` dependency management

### Testing Strategy
- Matrix testing using all existing pytest markers
- Coverage collection across all test types
- Optional slow test execution to maintain fast feedback
- Proper test isolation and environment setup

### Security Integration
- Seamless integration with existing security analysis script
- Bandit code scanning with confidence level reporting
- Safety dependency vulnerability scanning
- Security report artifacts with 90-day retention

### Docker Validation
- Complete build-to-runtime testing pipeline
- Health endpoint validation matching existing `/health` route
- API functionality testing using available transformations
- Graceful degradation when build environment restrictions exist

## Migration Strategy

- **Existing `test.yml`**: Renamed to `test-legacy.yml` and disabled to avoid conflicts
- **Existing `build.yml`**: Preserved for SonarQube integration (separate concern)
- **New `ci.yml`**: Comprehensive replacement providing all testing functionality

## Workflow Triggers

- Push to main branch
- Pull requests to main
- Manual dispatch with optional debug mode
- Smart slow test execution (main branch or labeled PRs)

## Artifacts and Reporting

- Coverage reports (HTML/XML) with 30-day retention
- Security analysis reports with 90-day retention
- Test results in JUnit format for GitHub integration
- Codecov integration for coverage tracking

This implementation provides a production-ready CI/CD foundation that ensures code quality, security, and functionality while maintaining fast feedback cycles for developers.

author: yancyribbens
body:
When fee-rate is high, using waste instead of weight creates an optimal sort order, leading to an optimal  solutions being found in less iterations.

The secondary sort order is used as a tie breaker when effective_values are equivalent.  Therefore, this optimization only is relevant given a pool with equivalent effective_values yet different waste scores.

When fee_rates are high, it's optimal to secondary sort by descending weight, and when fee_rates are low, it's optimal to secondary sort by ascending weight.  However, using a secondary sort by waste, it's always optimal to sort by ascending waste.

Consider the test `select_coins_bnb_effective_value_tie_high_fee_rate`. The optimal solution will be to use `UTXOs` with a lower weight when fee_rate is high.  The previous sort by descending weight gives

```
56/112 waste: 3
55/70 waste: 2
55/70 waste: 2
```

This leads to an un-optimal selection given the last two compose the optimal solution.  The optimal solution is still found, however not until the 7th iteration.

```
     []
    /
 56/112
  /
55/70
```

The solution is recorded here after the second iteration.  Next 55/70 is moved to the exclusion branch, however the next `UTXO` 55/70 is skipped because of the `UTXO` exclusion short-cut.  It's only after `56/112` is moved to the exclusion branch that the optimal solution is found

```
   []
     \
     56/112
      /
    55/70
     /
  55/70
```

By contrast, if the secondary sort is by waste, the optimal solution is found on the second iteration.

```
      []
     /
  55/70
   /
55/70
```

## HTTP Proxy Component: Configurable Request Router
This PR introduces a new HTTP proxy component that **prioritizes immediate Cat Voices proxying** while providing configurable request routing with a clear evolution path from simple external proxying to a sophisticated proxy system.
### 🚀 **Key Features**
**HTTP Proxy Component**
- Configurable HTTP proxy with regex-based routing engine
- **Immediate external redirect handling for Cat Voices endpoints** during transition period
- Static content serving with native response generation
- Comprehensive logging and error handling

### 📋 **Endpoint Coverage**
**Routes these patterns to external Cat Voices system for immediate proxying:**
- `/api/gateway/v1/config/frontend`
- `/api/gateway/v1/cardano/assets/*`
- `/api/gateway/v1/rbac/registration*`
- `/api/gateway/v1/document*` and `/api/gateway/v2/document*`



### ⚠️ **Static Assets Handling**
**Current State**: Static content handling (`/static/*` patterns) is implemented with placeholder responses only. The current implementation serves basic text responses for testing purposes. 

**Next PR Focus**: The immediate next PR will implement proper static asset serving for Flutter web assets and other static content. This includes:
- Asset file system integration
- Proper MIME type detection
- Caching headers and optimization
- Flutter web app serving capabilities

This separation allows the routing foundation to be established first, with static asset serving as a focused follow-up implementation.
### 🎯 **Current State → Vision**
**Currently serves as a temporary bridge ensuring immediate Cat Voices proxying** while providing the foundation for a sophisticated configurable proxy system with dynamic backend selection, health checks, and advanced traffic management.

body:
This PR completes the conversion from UUID-based to slug-based event routing while fixing critical database transaction issues that were causing test failures.

## Overview

Converts all event routes from UUID-based identifiers to human-readable slugs like `devfest-lille-2024`, providing better SEO, user experience, and URL stability. The implementation resolves database transaction context errors and ensures comprehensive test compatibility.

## Root Issue Fixed

**Problem**: "No transaction in context" errors occurring when repositories performed `EventEntity.findBySlug()` calls outside of transaction contexts after the slug-based conversion.

**Solution**: Systematically wrapped all database access patterns in proper transaction contexts and eagerly loaded entity relationships to prevent lazy loading issues.

## Key Changes

### Database Transaction Safety
Fixed transaction context issues across multiple repositories:

- **PartnershipAgreementRepositoryExposed**: Enhanced `generateAgreement()` to eagerly load all entity relationships (`event.organisation.representativeUser`, `option.option.translations`) within transaction context
- **PartnershipStorageRepositoryGoogleStorage**: Wrapped `uploadAgreement()` and `uploadSignedAgreement()` methods in `transaction {}` blocks
- **TicketRepositoryExposed**: Consolidated all database queries in `createTickets()` and `updateTicket()` within single transaction contexts

### Stable Event Slugs
Event slugs remain immutable after creation - updating an event's name no longer regenerates the slug, ensuring:
- Consistent URLs that don't break when event names change
- Better SEO and bookmark reliability
- Cleaner event lifecycle management

### Clean Repository Architecture
- All route handlers now depend on `EventRepository` interface instead of concrete implementations
- Removed direct `EventEntity` usage from route files
- Improved abstraction and testability

### Simplified Notification Handling
Converted `NotificationRepository.sendMessage` to accept `eventSlug` directly instead of `eventId`, eliminating redundant UUID lookups in route handlers.

## Test Results

**Before**: 10 failing tests with "No transaction in context" errors
**After**: All 171 tests passing (100% success rate)

The conversion maintains clean separation of concerns while providing better URLs, improved SEO, and more maintainable code with enhanced architectural boundaries and transaction safety.

# Pull Request Summary

## Enhanced Quota Token Contract with SIP-010 Compliance and Governance Timelock

### 🎯 **Overview**
This PR implements a comprehensive fishing quota token system on the Stacks blockchain with enterprise-grade features including SIP-010 fungible token compliance and democratic governance mechanisms for Total Allowable Catch (TAC) management.

### 📋 **Changes Summary**

#### **New Contract: `contracts/quota-token.clar`**
- **285 lines** of production-ready Clarity smart contract code
- Implements fungible token for fishing quota management
- SIP-010 standard compliance with full metadata support
- Governance timelock system for TAC changes

#### **Comprehensive Test Suite: `tests/quota-token.test.ts`**
- **215 lines** of TypeScript test code using Vitest + Clarinet SDK
- **9 test cases** covering all contract functionality
- **100% test coverage** of core features
- Event logging validation and error handling tests

### 🚀 **Key Features Implemented**

#### **Core Token Functionality**
```clarity
✅ Admin management (set-admin)
✅ TAC controls (set-tac with governance)
✅ Token minting (mint-quota within TAC limits)
✅ Quota allocation (allocate-quota to fishers)
✅ Token burning (burn-quota on catch)
✅ Peer-to-peer transfers (transfer between fishers)
```

#### **SIP-010 Fungible Token Standard**
```clarity
✅ get-name() -> "Fishing Quota Token"
✅ get-symbol() -> "QUOTA"
✅ get-decimals() -> 6
✅ get-token-uri() -> metadata URL
✅ get-balance(principal) -> response
✅ get-total-supply() -> response
✅ transfer(amount, sender, recipient, memo) -> SIP-010 compliant
```

#### **Governance Timelock System**
```clarity
✅ propose-tac(new-tac) -> Propose TAC changes

author: copilot
body:
The delete rules functionality was broken - when users tried to delete auto-generated rules, they would be immediately recreated from existing high-confidence AI transactions, making deletion appear ineffective.

## Problem
When deleting auto-generated rules through the Rules UI:
1. Rules would be deleted successfully via `rulesService.clearAllRules()`
2. The `loadRules()` function would immediately call `initializeRulesFromExistingTransactions()`
3. This would automatically recreate the same rules from existing transactions
4. Users would see the rules still there, thinking deletion failed

From the console logs in the issue:
```
📋 Auto-created rule for: OESTERBRO APOTEK (Capital One Venture) → Healthcare
📋 Auto-created rule for: AMAZON* WZ3I28L55 (Capital One Venture) → Shopping
```

This happened every time the Rules page was loaded, including after deletion operations.

## Solution
Modified `loadRules()` functions in both `Rules.tsx` and `CategoryRulesManager.tsx` to accept an optional `shouldAutoInitialize` parameter:

- **Default behavior preserved**: `loadRules()` defaults to `shouldAutoInitialize=true` for backward compatibility
- **After deletion**: Calls `loadRules(false)` to skip auto-initialization 
- **Explicit generation**: Users can still generate rules via the "Generate from Transactions" button

## Changes Made
- `src/components/Rules/Rules.tsx` - Added conditional auto-initialization logic
- `src/components/Transactions/CategoryRulesManager.tsx` - Applied same fix for individual rule deletions  
- `src/__tests__/deleteRulesNoAutoRecreateIssue.test.ts` - Added comprehensive test coverage

## Validation
✅ **Manual testing**: Rules can be deleted and stay deleted (no auto-recreation)  
✅ **Manual testing**: Explicit rule generation still works correctly  
✅ **All tests pass**: 443 tests including new regression test  
✅ **Build successful**: No compilation errors  
✅ **Backward compatibility**: All existing functionality preserved  

Fixes #453.

body:
This pull request introduces significant improvements to authentication, authorization, and project collaboration features in both the backend and frontend of the application. The changes enforce authentication for API routes, add fine-grained authorization checks for project actions, and enable project owners to manage collaborators. The frontend is updated to reflect these backend changes, providing a more user-aware and collaborative experience.

**Authentication & Authorization Enhancements**

* Added a new `authenticate` middleware in `middlewares.go` to enforce JWT authentication for protected routes, and updated all relevant routes in `routes.go` to use this middleware. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7279d82b7bad6c0433fb6b4a8f9e04cc76fe8944498cd5dcb21bd7f6bdabc36dR4-R68) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3f9b7f8459271513d7ad53e00c8495c1097cc1be28442a8ac9782a087cbc0133L15-R39)
* Implemented `requireUser` helper in `auth.go` and added authorization checks (owner/collaborator) for project-related actions, including creation, update, deletion, and viewing. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1c7069a8d19afafe9a1905dae4dcff4f3ebd390aff098e213c7cc24e4b247d77R12-R28) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7e7489dd9972b9bd9f2da6225c9c245a74103724932d7b1e7ec5970bc5a8ea1fR35-R39) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7e7489dd9972b9bd9f2da6225c9c245a74103724932d7b1e7ec5970bc5a8ea1fR76-R91) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-7e7489dd9972b9bd9f2da6225c9c245a74103724932d7b1e7ec5970bc5a8ea1fL95-R138) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-7e7489dd9972b9bd9f2da6225c9c245a74103724932d7b1e7ec5970bc5a8ea1fR194-R278) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-7e7489dd9972b9bd9f2da6225c9c245a74103724932d7b1e7ec5970bc5a8ea1fL189-R312)

**Project Collaboration Features**

* Added the ability for project owners to add collaborators via a new `addCollaboratorHandler` and corresponding API route. Collaborator checks are enforced for viewing and modifying projects. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7e7489dd9972b9bd9f2da6225c9c245a74103724932d7b1e7ec5970bc5a8ea1fR194-R278) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3f9b7f8459271513d7ad53e00c8495c1097cc1be28442a8ac9782a087cbc0133L15-R39)
* Updated project-related database interactions to associate projects with user IDs and retrieve only user-specific projects. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-7e7489dd9972b9bd9f2da6225c9c245a74103724932d7b1e7ec5970bc5a8ea1fL46-R53) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7e7489dd9972b9bd9f2da6225c9c245a74103724932d7b1e7ec5970bc5a8ea1fL189-R312)

**Frontend Updates for Collaboration and Authentication**

* Updated the `Projects` and `EditProject` components to conditionally render content based on authentication status, require input fields, and support adding collaborators via forms. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-93e2c746fe89960417d52032caf49bece4c8c22fd4c01c5c4d0c591c586ce07dL2-R11) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-93e2c746fe89960417d52032caf49bece4c8c22fd4c01c5c4d0c591c586ce07dR26-R39) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-035dcddd153f30eacc0164b9ba2d5fd4e63ac5b70b0cbc7c7bbcd1aff081ff43L4-R26)

**Token Handling Improvements**

* Improved token management in `authCallbackHandler` by deleting existing tokens before creating new ones, and enhanced JWT verification to return claims for downstream use. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-1c7069a8d19afafe9a1905dae4dcff4f3ebd390aff098e213c7cc24e4b247d77R79-R92) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1c7069a8d19afafe9a1905dae4dcff4f3ebd390aff098e213c7cc24e4b247d77L187-R223)

**Error Handling and Miscellaneous**

* Added a new `authorizationErrorResponse` for forbidden actions, and improved error messaging throughout the authentication and project handlers. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2dc3071ff01c04fb0536d6defa720916c679ec4c853c3891875710b745ce77b8R63-R66) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-7e7489dd9972b9bd9f2da6225c9c245a74103724932d7b1e7ec5970bc5a8ea1fR76-R91) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-7e7489dd9972b9bd9f2da6225c9c245a74103724932d7b1e7ec5970bc5a8ea1fL95-R138)

These changes collectively strengthen the security model, enable user collaboration on projects, and improve the overall user experience in both the backend API and frontend UI.
